meaning: The number of Benjamites living in Jerusalem after the return from exile (1 Chron. 9:9)
description: The number 956 appears in 1 Chronicles 9:9, where it states that 956 men from the tribe of Benjamin were settled in Jerusalem after returning from the Babylonian exile. These men are described as heads of their ancestral houses and represented a significant portion of the rebuilding community. The context in 1 Chronicles 9 is an overview of those who first returned to their properties and cities, with special emphasis on the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, Manasseh, as well as the Levites and priests. The number highlights the role of the tribe of Benjamin in the renewed settlement of the holy city after the exile.

versions.meaning: The number 956 has no known or established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: In biblical numerology and Jewish gematria, certain numbers carry strong symbolic significance, such as 7 (perfection), 12 (the tribes of Israel), and 40 (testing). The number 956 is not among these and holds no specific symbolic role in the Bible or in traditional Jewish mysticism. It could potentially be analyzed through gematria by finding Hebrew words with the same numerical value, but there is no widely recognized or established interpretation linked to this number.
versions.reason: [major] The number 956 appears explicitly in 1 Chronicles 9:9 as the count of Benjaminites living in Jerusalem after the exile. This is an important biblical reference that should be included in description and meaning.; [major] The Meaning field states that the number has no known significance in biblical tradition, but it occurs concretely in the Bible as a specific figure linked to the tribe of Benjamin in Jerusalem following the return from Babylon.; [minor] A footnote on the historical context for 1 Chronicles 9 (the rebuilding of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile) would enrich the description.

footnotes.text: 1 Chronicles 9 is considered one of the most important genealogical texts in the Old Testament, as it documents who first returned from the Babylonian exile and restored the Jewish community in Jerusalem.

The tribe of Benjamin had a special connection to Jerusalem, since the city lay on the border between Judah and Benjamin. After the kingdom was divided, Benjamin remained loyal to the kingdom of Judah and the temple in Jerusalem.
The parallel passage in Nehemiah 11:7–8 gives a slightly different number for the Benjamites in Jerusalem, reflecting differences in time period or counting criteria between the two sources.
